claims.text: The studied alloy is Co-free equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Rate- and temperature-dependent dislocation mobility predominantly determines the dynamic strength–ductility balance of equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Lower temperatures and higher strain rates inhibit dislocation climb and cross-slip in FeNiCrMn.
The inhibition of climb and cross-slip is related to the alloy's intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
Inhibited dislocation mechanisms increase yield strength and alter work-hardening behavior.
Dislocation accumulation is the key structural mediator of dynamic mechanical performance.
Rapid solidification produces a homogeneous, single-phase FCC FeNiCrMn microstructure.
The FCC phase remains stable over the proposed temperature range of approximately 77–773 K and strain-rate range of 10^-3–10^3 s^-1.
Changes in dislocation density and arrangement within the FCC matrix mediate the observed mechanical response.
Temperature and strain rate modulate dislocation motion and interactions through the alloy's intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
Higher strain rates and lower temperatures will produce increased dislocation pile-ups and reduced recovery.
Minimal or secondary twin formation would support dislocation kinetics as the dominant mechanism.
Significant twin activity dominating the mechanical response would challenge the proposed mechanism.
The hypothesis applies only while the FCC structure is retained and no stress-induced phase transformation occurs.
Extremely high strain rates or temperatures may activate twinning-induced plasticity or phase transformation.
A lack of correlation between mechanical changes and dislocation mobility, or dominance by twinning or another mechanism, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Twinning-induced plasticity is declared outside the hypothesis boundary, but dominant twinning is also presented as a result that would challenge or falsify the hypothesis. This permits the same observation to be treated either as falsification or as an out-of-scope condition.

The conditions state that the entire proposed test matrix remains within stable FCC behavior, while the boundary acknowledges that extreme rates or temperatures may activate mechanisms or transformations outside that regime; no numerical boundary is given to distinguish these cases.
